title: Indus Valley Civilization found by railway workers
place_text: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, Indus River, Pakistan

tellings.quote: accidental Discovery uh Railway workers building a railway line that actually led to that

plain: The ancient Indus Valley civilization, with its cities at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa in what is now Pakistan, was found by accident in the 1920s, when railway workers building a line stumbled onto its remains. The writer Graham Hancock, known for his theories of lost ancient civilizations, mentions this to Michels without naming a source, as an example of how whole civilizations can lie undiscovered.
